description: Participants learn inference by computing it. On synthetic data from a fictional water utility whose true population is known, they draw repeated samples, build bootstrap intervals, run permutation tests beside classical ones, and report effect sizes with intervals instead of bare p-values. They see how testing 30 districts at once produces false findings and correct for it, then fit and read a first linear regression.
audience: Practitioners. Graduates and early-career analysts who have completed the FN courses or passed the placement test, and analysts moving into data science.
prerequisites: FN-101 Python for Data and AI Work
FN-103 Mathematics for Machine Learning: Vectors, Gradients and Probability
Filters and groups a table with a dataframe library
Computes a mean, a standard deviation and a simple probability

outcomes.text: Explain what a sampling distribution, a standard error, a confidence interval and a p-value describe, and identify common misreadings, given eight statements from utility reports
outcomes.evidence: a marked sheet with reasons, at least six of eight correct

outcomes.text: Compute bootstrap intervals for a mean, a median and a group difference, resampling the correct unit, given skewed repair times with the population known
outcomes.evidence: each interval with its coverage over 1,000 simulated samples

outcomes.text: Implement a permutation test, compare it with the matching classical test and report an effect size with an interval, given satisfaction scores for two contractors
outcomes.evidence: a script reporting both p-values and the effect size

outcomes.text: Apply family-wise and false discovery rate corrections to many tests and measure the false findings without them, given 30 districts of unequal size, five with a planted difference
outcomes.evidence: true and false discoveries under no correction, Holm and Benjamini-Hochberg

outcomes.text: Analyse a linear regression of water consumption on household size and temperature, with slope intervals and residual checks, given 2,000 synthetic metered households
outcomes.evidence: a regression summary, a residual plot and a two-sentence interpretation

outcomes.text: Deliver an inference brief that answers a manager's question with an estimate, an interval, a test, an effect size and stated limits, given a question and a dataset not seen in class
outcomes.evidence: a two-page brief and a notebook that reruns from raw data, defended live
